items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: She had a good band if we could play. See here's the thing about Blanche's band. They had some very good players in there. Boy by the name of Booker Pittman on the clarinet and saxophone... I had to catch her on the cymbals.

ctx.x: And he said something to the effect--I can't quote exactly--he said something to the effect that Blanche had a band as good as any man's.

She had a good band if we could play. See here's the thing about Blanche's band. They had some very good players in there. Boy by the name of Booker Pittman on the clarinet and saxophone, very fast tongue for tonguing alto and clarinet; Ben Webster, very good; Edgar Battle, trumpet. Well see, Blanche would be in front of the band and we used to do a number like "I Need Loving," (HUMMING). Well anyway, Blanche would be in front of the band dancing. Well, if Ben had a solo or any one of the musicians had a solo to…

catch her on the cymbals. Well see, well that's very unprofessional with Ben Webster taking a solo and you're up there trying to catch Blanche Calloway when she's kicking her legs upin the air on the cymbal. You know that was one of the troubles.
